metadata.title: What Actually Happens When Claude "Initiates Coverage"?
metadata.purpose: Answer whether asking Claude to initiate coverage on a company means it writes the whole research report in one pass -- or is doing something more structured. Lands the carry-out that the workflow is five fixed, dependency-gated tasks, and a finished report means the chain completed, not that a person checked the assumptions inside it.

beats.narration_text: Someone asks whether initiating coverage means Claude produces the whole report instantly, in one pass. It doesn't. Liam is here to take you through exactly how the skill actually works, task by task.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'What produces the report -- instantly?', hesitates on 'instantly', corrects to 'five ordered tasks', lands the real question

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('instantly' -> 'five ordered tasks') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: The natural guess is that initiating coverage means Claude writes the whole report in one continuous pass, choosing whatever order makes sense. But the skill runs five fixed tasks, in order -- company research, financial modeling, valuation analysis, chart generation, and final report assembly -- each one executed individually with its prerequisite verified first. Ask it to jump straight to valuation before a financial model exists, and there's nothing to value: task three's prerequisite isn't there, so it can't run.

shot.new_visual_element: A one-pass generator, struck; a five-task ordered chain, lit

production_viz.label: One pass, struck -- five tasks, lit
production_viz.mechanic: Left: a single card labelled 'ONE PASS' with a report icon appearing instantly beneath it. Right: a card labelled 'FIVE TASKS, IN ORDER' listing three grouped lines. The one-pass side dims and gets a terracotta strike; the five-task side stays lit. A final line reads 'valuation before a model exists -- can't run' and the chain does not reach for it.

beats.narration_text: What the skill actually does: task one produces company research as a markdown document, task two builds a financial model in Excel, task three runs valuation analysis from that model's numbers, task four generates charts, and task five assembles everything into a final report as a Word document. Watch the anchor: one ticker's coverage package moving through all five tasks, in order. Each task waits until the deliverable before it exists and has been verified, before it starts.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- one ticker's coverage package traveling through RESEARCH -> MODEL -> VALUATION -> CHARTS -> REPORT, in order

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- one package, five tasks
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Five stacked cards labelled 'RESEARCH', 'MODEL', 'VALUATION', 'CHARTS', 'REPORT'. A single highlighted token 'TICKER PACKAGE' travels down through all five cards in turn, each lighting as it arrives, never skipping ahead of an unlit card. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS, PAID OFF, AT B03.

beats.narration_text: The coverage package comes out the other side as a finished report -- but every task along the way ran only because the one before it had already produced a verified deliverable. That proves the order was respected: no step started on an input that wasn't there yet. It doesn't prove the analysis inside each step was sound -- a financial model can pass verification with unrealistic growth assumptions built into it. And if a task can't start because an earlier deliverable isn't ready, that's a sequencing gap, not evidence that the earlier research itself was bad.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS, resting at REPORT; splits into 'ran is not sound' and 'blocked is not bad'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- report, then split
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 FIVE-CARD COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical placement, the token resting at the 'REPORT' card. It shrinks and slides up. Two cards fade in beneath: left reads 'RAN: VALUATION' with a checkmark, then a struck-through 'SOUND?' beneath it, labelled 'ran is not sound'; right reads 'BLOCKED: TASK 3' beside a faint 'model missing, not wrong' note, labelled 'blocked is not bad'.

beats.narration_text: Initiating coverage doesn't mean Claude writes a report in one pass -- it runs five fixed tasks, in order, and each one is blocked until the task before it hands over a verified deliverable. A finished report means the chain completed end to end, not that a person checked the assumptions inside it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt -- read it with me. Pick a public company you know. Ask Claude to do three things in order: research the company, sketch a simple financial projection, then value it from that projection -- and have it show you each step's output before starting the next. Then ask it to skip straight to the valuation without the projection step, and watch what happens. Liam, in for Bear.
